Figure 2. Illustration of the proposed FedVLA framework and its key component. (a) An overview of the FedVLA, which consists of
multiple clients and a server. Each client processes vision-language-action inputs through the Stem, Trunk, and Head modules. Clients send
their updated trunk parameters to the server, where Expert-Driven Aggregation selectively integrates expert-specific updates on server. The
global trunk module is then distributed to clients for the next training round. (b) Details of the proposed Dual Gating MoE module. The
input tokens first pass through the token-level gate Gt , computing the gating scores for each expert with residual scores from the previous
MoE layer. Only the computed scores surpass the expert-level gate Ge , activating the corresponding expert to process the token. Finally,
the expert outputs are combined to generate the final output tokens.

Implementation Details. We validate our FedVLA in both               more, FedVLA consistently outperforms FedAvg, which
simulation and real-world scenarios, where each client per-          only achieves an average success rate of 51.7%. This per-
forms a single task, resulting in a non-iid data distribution.       formance gap can be attributed to FedAvg overlooking task
We employ the pretrained HPT [28] as the backbone of our             heterogeneity in federated learning. In contrast, FedVLA
VLA model and train it for 1,000 communication rounds                explicitly accounts for task heterogeneity during aggrega-
between clients and the server, with each client performing          tion by leveraging expert-driven model updates, ensuring
local training for 5 epochs per round. In simulation, the            that knowledge from diverse clients is effectively integrated
model is trained with a learning rate of 5 × 10−6 , while in         to enhance generalization across different tasks.
real-world settings, the learning rate is set to 2×10−5 . Each
client trains locally with a batch size of 256 using the Adam        4.2. Real-World
optimizer. The experiments are conducted on a workstation

   Figure 6. Visualization of expert activation distribution per task for different object types. The x-axis represents the three object groups
   (target objects, surrounding objects, and background objects), where each group contains eight sub-bars corresponding to different experts
   selected. The left y-axis indicates the activation count, showing how frequently experts are selected for each object type. The right y-
   axis represents the density of experts per token, illustrating the average number of experts assigned per token in each object category.
   The dashed line represents the average expert density per token across different object groups, highlighting the dynamic expert selection
   mechanism of DGMoE.


   4.4. Analysis on DGMoE                                                                                                                                                                5. Conclusion
   The DGMoE is designed to enhance model efficiency by                                                                                                                                  In this work, we introduced FedVLA, a novel federated
   selectively activating experts based on task complexity and                                                                                                                           vision-language action learning framework that preserves
   their corresponding object types. In contrast, supporting                                                                                                                             privacy and effectively balances data privacy and task per-
   objects and background objects, which provide contextual                                                                                                                              formance. To address the challenges of task heterogeneity
   spatial information, activate fewer experts compared to tar-                                                                                                                          and efficient knowledge aggregation in decentralized set-
   get objects. Notably, target objects tend to activate experts                                                                                                                         tings, we proposed three key components: the Instruction-
   4, 7, and 8 more frequently, supporting objects prefer to se-                                                                                                                         Oriented Scene-Parsing module, which enhances feature
   lect experts 6, 7, and 8, whereas background objects favor                                                                                                                            extraction by decomposing raw observations into struc-
   experts 2, 3, and 5. This demonstrates that DGMoE not                                                                                                                                 tured object-level representations guided by task instruc-
   only dynamically allocates computational resources based                                                                                                                              tions. The Dual Gating Mixture-of-Experts, which intro-
   on object relevance but also selectively routes information                                                                                                                           duces self-aware experts capable of bidirectional token se-
   to specialized experts, enhancing efficiency and adaptability                                                                                                                         lection, optimizing computational efficiency while preserv-
   across different object categories.                                                                                                                                                   ing task performance, and the Expert-Driven Aggregation
      Furthermore, we quantitatively measure the average ex-                                                                                                                             strategy, which dynamically assigns aggregation weights
   pert density per token across different tasks, also as shown                                                                                                                          based on expert similarity across clients. Extensive ex-
   in Figure 6. The proposed DGMoE achieves consistently                                                                                                                                 periments in both simulated and real-world environments
   lower expert activation densities compared to vanilla top-                                                                                                                            demonstrate that FedVLA achieves performance compara-
   k MoE, which assigns tokens to a fixed number of experts,                                                                                                                             ble to centralized training while ensuring privacy protec-
   where k is typically an integer greater than one. The average                                                                                                                         tion. We believe these results may contribute to the develop-
   number of activated experts per token is 1.219, 1.229, 1.225,                                                                                                                         ment of more generalizable and scalable federated learning
   and 1.227 for Open Drawer, Sorting Pills, Trash Collection,                                                                                                                           frameworks for robotic manipulation.
   and Clean Up, respectively. Such dynamic and sparse acti-
   vation directly translates into significantly reduced forward-                                                                                                                        Acknowledgements. This research was supported by
   pass computation, making DGMoE especially suitable for                                                                                                                                Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation
   deployment on resource-constrained edge devices.                                                                                                                                      (No. 2024A1515011774).
